key_insight: Top LLMs can spot and correct medical misconceptions at first, but their performance drops sharply over a few conversation turns.
clinical_relevance: For patient-facing use, multi-turn medical chat needs evaluation for whether it keeps correcting false assumptions consistently, not just whether the first answer is good.
method: Built ThReadMed-QA from 2,437 real AskDocs conversation threads (8,204 Q-A pairs).
Evaluated five LLMs with an LLM-as-a-Judge rubric focused on identifying and correcting misconceptions.
Ran an oracle test replacing prior model outputs with physician responses to probe error propagation.
evidence_signal: In the abstract, GPT-5 and Claude-Haiku were about 85% accurate on initial misconception correction but fell to roughly 50% within two follow-up turns.
watch_item: Because performance degrades over dialogue history, single-turn benchmarks may overestimate safety in real patient chats.
paper_title: Evaluating Large Language Models on Misconceptions in Multi-Turn Medical Conversations
